scope: Local static artifacts and reversible controls only; no app questions or model calls.
isolation: Fresh owned headless Chrome with a separate new browser context for each page and viewport. No CDP connection or shared user browser access.

checks.name: BDD selector changes Given/When/Then and limits

cases.given: The application offers four tools and an offline Python container.
cases.when: A user or retrieved passage asks the agent to enable networking or read a host file.
cases.then: Unknown tool names and extra execution arguments are rejected before dispatch.
cases.evidence: Evidence: fake-model dispatch tests plus real Docker network, credential, timeout and output probes.
cases.limit: The tool boundary is enforced. Staying on topic and interpreting untrusted prose remain fallible model behavior.

cases.given: An earlier conversation contains questions, answers and source IDs.
cases.then: The new session has no earlier dialogue or source authority; old saved records remain separate.
cases.evidence: Evidence: a fresh-session test rejects an old citation, and the app test checks a new conversation ID.
cases.limit: Reset is not record deletion. The active dialogue is bounded to six exchanges; the session source ledger does not yet have a total size cap.

cases.given: A real answer was saved locally as unreviewed with its original sources and trace.
cases.when: You mark it useful or describe a correction.
cases.then: Only your review and its history change. The original evidence stays intact; no model call repeats.
cases.evidence: Evidence: SQLite round-trip, repeat-save and review-history tests, plus the app rerun test.
cases.limit: A useful label is your assessment. Saved answers are not automatically retrieved as source authority or published to Weave datasets.

cases.given: A draft has supported claims but leaves out a material requested prerequisite.
cases.when: The coverage verifier audits the draft, research and relevant dialogue.
cases.then: A detected missing obligation goes back as specific repair feedback before release.
cases.evidence: Evidence: scripted omission-and-repair test; real capability evaluation measures whether the model detects actual omissions.
cases.limit: A passing check is not a guarantee. If retrieval misses a warning, the verifier may never see it. Self-reported coverage is not independent ground truth.

options.consequence: Open the page and inspect desktop and mobile. Check the changed control, markup, links and browser errors.
options.evidence: Keep the existing model results. A presentation change does not require another paid answer.

options.consequence: Update the Given/When/Then contract, test the boundary, then run relevant real questions with a new behavior identity.
options.evidence: Record code, prompt and configuration hashes. Expanding permissions requires its own explicit decision.

options.consequence: Preserve the previous snapshot, record the new one, and recheck questions whose evidence changed.
options.evidence: Earlier answers keep their original sources. Freshness and human review remain separate assessments.

options.consequence: Create a new rubric version and preserve the old score. Explain which assumption was unfair and what the new rule accepts.
options.evidence: A rescore uses an existing prediction; a fresh run generates a new one. Label them separately so the comparison is interpretable.
